service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events in the Colorado mountain corridor, solo through quartet, with travel and lodging itemised as their own lines.

faqs.q: What does the resort need to provide?
faqs.a: One or two dedicated 20-amp circuits within reach of the performance area, not shared with catering warmers or a lighting truss, which is the most common cause of a setup problem. Setup runs 45 to 90 minutes depending on size, pack-down 30 to 60, timed to the dock and elevator windows the venue gives us.

faqs.q: How loud is it, and do you honor sound caps and curfews?
faqs.a: The welcome dinner plays at the level of the conversation, and the last night plays like a dance band. Mountain venues run their own rules, so tell us the cap and the curfew when you book and both go into the plan, with the set built to land on the curfew.

faqs.q: Can the band play outdoors at altitude?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it and a move-indoors call time written before the day, because mountain evenings drop fast. The corridor runs from about 7,900 feet in Aspen to roughly 9,600 in Breckenridge, where singers and horns pace a night differently and the temperature swing means more retuning.

faqs.q: Do you play company offsites for remote and hybrid teams?
faqs.a: Yes, and the offsite is now the most common reason a company books a mountain evening. Tell us the dates, the venue and roughly how many are flying in, and we'll plan every evening of the stay on one contract.
